meta.title: US natural gas price-spike episodes vs storage conditions
meta.purpose: Calibration dataset for a convex price-response function: price as a function of Lower 48 working-gas storage deviation from the 5-year average.

units.prices: USD per MMBtu (nominal, EIA Henry Hub spot unless noted)
units.storage: Bcf, Lower 48 working gas (EIA Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report)
units.storage_dev_pct: percent deviation from the trailing 5-year average for the same week

method_notes: Monthly average Henry Hub prices are from EIA's official monthly spot series (rngwhhdM).

Storage deviations are the figures EIA published in the Natural Gas Weekly Update / Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report for the stated week; entries flagged approx are estimated from EIA articles rather than an exact WNGSR line.

Key lesson encoded in this data: MONTHLY AVERAGE price tracks the storage deficit (convex), while DAILY spikes are dominated by short-lived demand/supply shocks (freeze-offs, hurricanes) and can hit extreme levels even with storage in surplus (e.g., Jan 2026 record $30.72 with storage +6% pre-storm).

episodes.name: Winter 2014 polar vortex

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: By Feb 5 HH hit $7.90, its highest since Sep 24, 2008 (EIA NGW).

episodes.cause: Repeated arctic outbreaks drove record heating demand and record seasonal withdrawals (~3 Tcf), with Northeast pipeline constraints producing $100+ regional blowouts.

episodes.name: January 2018 bomb cyclone (Winter Storm Grayson)

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: fell back to $3.11 by Jan 10 (EIA NGW)

transco_zone6_ny.note: all-time-record daily average; intraday trades reported up to $175/MMBtu (NGI)

episodes.cause: Explosive East Coast cyclogenesis spiked demand to record ~134 Bcf/d against constrained Northeast pipelines; national benchmark barely moved on a monthly basis because storage was only moderately short.

episodes.name: February 2021 Winter Storm Uri

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: up from $3.76 on Feb 10; then-record in EIA daily series

ogt_oklahoma.note: Oklahoma intrastate next-day gas traded from ~$3 to ~$1,200/MMBtu, the most extreme North American gas print on record

waha.note: all-time record for the hub (EIA NGW)

mid_episode.note: 338 Bcf withdrawal, 2nd-largest ever; record 156 Bcf draw in South Central region

episodes.cause: Deep freeze into Texas froze wellheads and gathering systems (largest monthly US production decline on record) exactly as heating/power demand peaked; physical scarcity on intrastate systems produced 3-4 digit prices despite only a ~8% national storage deficit.

episodes.name: 2022 post-Russia-invasion run

peak_deficit.note: largest deficit of the refill season

ttf_peak.note: TTF settled ~EUR 339-343/MWh (~USD 100/MMBtu at 3.412 MMBtu/MWh and ~parity FX) - a near-total storage-security panic price; TTF weekly average was $77.60/MMBtu in the Aug 18-24 week (EIA NGW)

episodes.cause: Record LNG exports pulling US gas into a Europe scrambling to replace Russian pipeline supply, a persistent 12-17% US storage deficit, and a hot summer kept Henry Hub at $7-10 for months - a storage/depletion-driven (not weather-shock) episode.

episodes.name: December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: December 2022 daily high came in pre-storm cold; during Elliott the national benchmark stayed in the $5-7 range while regional cash blew out

western_hubs.note: several western hubs averaged >$48/MMBtu ABOVE Henry Hub

mid_episode.note: 213 Bcf withdrawal (EIA storage dashboard); deviation approximated from dashboard scatter (~-200 to -215 Bcf)

episodes.cause: A continent-scale flash freeze days before Christmas cut production >15 Bcf/d (Appalachia -27% or more) while demand spiked, forcing grid emergencies in the East; effects faded within a week so the monthly average barely registered.

episodes.name: 2005 Hurricanes Katrina/Rita

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: Louisiana-average cash $13.45 on Sep 28 while Henry Hub itself was shut in by Rita; daily spot prints of $15+ reported post-Rita; NYMEX front-month hit an intraday record $15.78 on Dec 13, 2005

mid_episode.note: storage was ABOVE the 5-year average during the spike

episodes.cause: Back-to-back hurricanes shut in up to ~77% of Gulf of Mexico gas output (~8-10 Bcf/d; 140+ Bcf cumulative by late Sep), a pure pre-shale supply shock: prices tripled to $13-15 with storage in surplus, showing that flow scarcity, not inventory, set the price.

episodes.name: Winter 2000-01 price peak (pre-shale scarcity + California crisis)

california_border.note: daily spot reached $69/MMBtu (then a national record) during the California power crisis; CA daily prices AVERAGED ~$15 (FRBSF)

mid_episode.note: record-cold Nov-Dec drove the largest net withdrawals then measured; stocks entered winter at their lowest level since the 1970s and sat at record seasonal lows (~15-20% below normal) through Dec-Jan (GAO-03-46)

episodes.cause: Flat pre-shale production ran into demand growth and record November-December cold with storage already at record lows - the first demonstration of the modern convex price response to inventory scarcity.

episodes.name: Mid-2008 price peak (commodity supercycle)
episodes.cause: $145 oil, global LNG pull, and pre-shale supply anxiety carried gas to $13+ with storage only ~3% below normal - evidence that the pre-shale price LEVEL was a regime effect, not a storage-deviation effect.

episodes.name: Mid-January 2025 arctic outbreak

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: highest since January 2024; back to $3.89 by Jan 22

mid_episode.note: 223 Bcf withdrawal; storage still slightly ABOVE the 5-year average

episodes.cause: Sharp but brief national cold snap (including the Gulf Coast snow event): multi-day daily-price spike with essentially normal storage, so the monthly average stayed near $4.

episodes.name: January 2026 Winter Storm Fern - all-time Henry Hub daily record

henry_hub_peak_spot.note: all-time nominal daily record in EIA/LSEG data, surpassing Uri's $23.86; NGI assessed a record $30.565 on Jan 26, Argus $28.00 on Jan 26; $8.15 on Jan 22 and $9.03 on Jan 28 bookended the blowout

henry_hub_monthly_avg.note: Jan 2026 avg +81% vs Dec; highest monthly average since 2022

pre_storm.note: storage was in SURPLUS before the storm (about +6% mid-January)

record_draw_week.note: 360 Bcf withdrawal - largest in WNGSR history (89% / ~170 Bcf above the 5-yr avg draw); level derived as 2,823 - 360

end_of_season.note: season withdrawals 2,048 Bcf, +5% vs 5-yr avg; deficit fully rebuilt by end of winter

episodes.cause: Extreme cold, snow and ice from New Mexico to New England pushed res/comm demand 29% above the 5-year average while freeze-offs cut production up to ~17 Bcf/d (rivaling Uri), on top of record ~20 Bcf/d LNG exports; the record daily print occurred with storage in surplus, then prices collapsed to $3.62 (Feb) and $3.04 (Mar) as the deficit peaked at only ~6%.

pre_shale_2000_2008.note: Structurally scarce: flat conventional production, oil-linked pricing psychology; $10-15 peaks occurred with storage near normal.

shale_era_2012_2024.note: Supply-elastic: shale caps the monthly price response; even -20% storage deficits produced $6-9, not $13-15. 2024 was the record-low annual average; 2025 averaged $3.52. Real values use approximate CPI-U deflation to 2025 dollars.
shale_era_2012_2024.emerging_note: 2025-2026: record LNG exports (~20+ Bcf/d) and data-center power demand are re-tightening the regime; Jan 2026 monthly avg $7.72 was the highest since 2022 and the $30.72 daily print was an all-time record.

price_vs_storage.description: Observation pairs for curve fitting: x = Lower 48 working-gas deviation from the 5-year average (fraction, + = surplus) in/near the price month; y = monthly average Henry Hub spot ($/MMBtu, nominal). regime: 'shale' or 'pre_shale'. Entries with approx=true use EIA-article-derived rather than exact WNGSR deviations.

observations.note: warm winter surplus; near-record-low real prices
deepest post-Fern deficit; price already mean-reverting
peak refill-season deficit -367 Bcf (wk 2022-08-12); TTF ~$100/MMBtu analog
bomb cyclone; brief shock, deficit not yet priced as persistent

observations.outlier: end-of-season deficit; forward market already pricing the injection-season rebuild, so monthly price relaxed despite the deepest deficit on record
Fern demand shock: monthly avg (and record $30.72 daily) driven by flow scarcity with storage near normal
Katrina/Rita supply shock with storage in surplus

suggested_fit.form: P = a * exp(-b * dev), dev = fractional deviation from 5-yr average (surplus positive)

piecewise_slopes.note: log-price slope is ~50% steeper on the deficit side - convexity beyond a single exponential

guidance: Fit on shale-era monthly observations only; add ~+$6-7 level shift (or a multiplicative ~2.5x) for pre-shale-style regimes.
Apply the curve to MID-WINTER deficits; end-of-season deficits (Mar 2014) under-price because the market discounts the coming rebuild.

Overlay a separate short-duration demand-shock term for daily/weekly spikes: freeze-off events produced daily prints of 3x-8x the monthly average ($23.86 Uri, $30.72 Fern) largely independent of the storage state.
Regional basis (Transco Z6/Algonquin $78-175; Texas intrastate $200-1,200) is a pipeline-constraint phenomenon, not a storage phenomenon - model separately.
